findings.title: query output is human-prose only — no --json / structured mode
findings.why_it_matters: run_query() writes formatted multi-line prose blocks to stdout with embedded labels like '[1] chunk_id=... score=... source=...'. An agent consuming query results must parse free text with brittle string splitting. Any cosmetic change (label reordering, whitespace, Japanese text) silently breaks the agent's parser. There is no --json flag, no --format flag, and no auto-detection of non-TTY stdout to switch to machine-readable output.
evidence: query.py:151-157: print(f'\n[{i}] chunk_id={hit.chunk_id} score={hit.score:.4f} source={hit.source}') and two more print() calls per hit, all to stdout, no structured alternative
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--format {human,json}` (default `human` for TTY, `json` when not `sys.stdout.isatty()`). In json mode, `json.dumps([{'rank':i,'chunk_id':h.chunk_id,'score':h.score,'source':h.source,'text':h.text,'top_keywords':h.top_keywords} for i,h in enumerate(result.hits,1)], ensure_ascii=False)` to stdout; all diagnostic/warn messages stay on stderr. argparse: `p.add_argument('--format', choices=['human','json'], default=None)` then resolve default at runtime with `sys.stdout.isatty()` check.

findings.title: lint exit code is binary (0/1) — warnings indistinguishable from clean pass
findings.why_it_matters: run_lint() returns exit 0 when there are zero FATAL findings, regardless of how many WARNING findings exist. An agent wiring `chunking lint` into a quality gate cannot distinguish 'clean corpus' from 'corpus with 20 duplicate-chunk warnings'. The plan explicitly specifies fatal=2, warning=1, success=0 but the implementation collapses fatal>0 to 1 and everything else to 0. Agents scripting `if exit_code == 1: trigger_reindex` cannot work.
evidence: lint.py:293: `return 0 if report.count(FATAL) == 0 else 1` — warnings return 0, fatals return 1, no exit code 2 used at all
findings.suggested_fix: Align with the plan: `if report.count(FATAL): return 2; if report.count(WARNING): return 1; return 0`. Document in the argparse help for the lint subcommand: add an epilog string `'Exit codes: 0=clean, 1=warnings only, 2=fatal findings'` via `p.formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter` and `p.epilog='...'`.

findings.title: lint has no --format json — machine parsing requires regex over Japanese prose
findings.why_it_matters: All lint output goes to stderr as Japanese-language prose lines like '[致命] missing_artifact: 必要成果物が存在しません'. An agent must scrape Japanese severity labels from stderr to count fatal/warning items, which is fragile. lint.md is written as a Markdown table — also not parseable without a Markdown parser. A --format json mode emitting structured {severity, category, message, detail} records would let agents filter, count, or react to specific categories without text parsing.
evidence: lint.py:296-304: _print_human_report() writes all findings to stderr as '[{f.severity}] {f.category}: {f.message}', no JSON alternative
lint.py:307-329: _write_lint_md() writes Markdown table to disk, no JSON equivalent on stdout
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--format {human,json}` to the lint subparser. In json mode: print `json.dumps({'summary':{'fatal':N,'warning':W,'info':I},'findings':[{'severity':f.severity,'category':f.category,'message':f.message,'detail':f.detail} for f in report.findings]}, ensure_ascii=False)` to stdout; suppress _print_human_report. TTY auto-detect as default.

findings.title: ingest success summary and all operational messages go to stderr — no machine-readable stdout signal on success
findings.why_it_matters: On success, run_ingest() prints 'ingest OK: N chunks from M files -> output_dir' to stderr (line 452-457). There is no stdout output at all on the happy path. An agent chaining `ingest` into a pipeline cannot capture the chunk count or output path without parsing stderr, which is mixed with [warn] and [error] lines. A JSON summary on stdout (or at minimum a parseable single-line stdout success record) lets agents confirm ingest results without touching stderr.
evidence: ingest.py:452-457: `print(f'ingest OK: ...', file=sys.stderr)` — success confirmation written to stderr, stdout is silent
findings.suggested_fix: On success (exit_code==0), write a JSON summary to stdout: `json.dumps({'status':'ok','chunks':result.chunks_generated,'input_files':result.total_input_files - result.skipped_files,'output_dir':str(cfg.output_dir),'wiki':dataclasses.asdict(result.wiki_stats) if result.wiki_stats else None}, ensure_ascii=False)`. Keep human prose on stderr. A `--quiet` flag can suppress the stderr banner. argparse: `p.add_argument('--quiet', action='store_true', help='stderr 出力を抑制')`.

findings.title: ingest exit codes 2-10 are undocumented in help text and README
findings.why_it_matters: ingest uses exit codes 2 (no input files), 3 (LLM backend unavailable), 4 (analyzer init failed), 5 (0 chunks produced), 6 (wiki generation aborted), 10 (unexpected exception). An agent must know whether to retry, fix configuration, or escalate. Without a documented code table, the agent must treat every non-zero exit as an opaque failure and request human intervention. Code 10 (generic exception) in particular gives no retry guidance.
evidence: ingest.py:122 exit_code=2 (no .txt files), 133 exit_code=3 (LLM), 163 exit_code=4 (analyzer), 196 exit_code=5 (0 chunks), 253 exit_code=6 (wiki), 280 exit_code=10 (exception)
cli.py _add_ingest(): no epilog documenting these codes
findings.suggested_fix: Add `p.epilog` to _add_ingest() (and _add_query(), _add_lint()) with a terse exit-code table. Use `p.formatter_class = argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter`. Example: 'Exit codes: 0=success 2=no input files 3=LLM unavailable 4=analyzer init failed 5=zero chunks 6=wiki aborted 10=unexpected error'. Mirror in README.md under a '## Exit codes' section.

findings.title: query "no matching chunks" returns exit 0 — agent cannot distinguish empty result from error
findings.why_it_matters: When q_vec.nnz==0 (query outside vocabulary) or when score filtering produces zero hits, run_query() prints '(no matching chunks)' to stderr and returns exit 0. In --json mode (not yet implemented) this means an agent receives empty output on stdout with exit 0 and must parse stderr to detect the empty-results case vs. actual 0-chunk corpus. A distinct exit code (e.g. 4) for 'query succeeded but no hits' allows agents to branch without stderr parsing.
evidence: query.py:148-150: `print('(no matching chunks)', file=sys.stderr); return 0` — zero-hit treated same as successful hits
query.py:103-109: q_vec.nnz==0 path also returns exit_code=0 with error_message set but hits=[]
findings.suggested_fix: Return exit code 4 (or a documented constant) when result.hits is empty after a successful query (artifacts loaded, no load errors). Document: '0=hits returned, 2=artifacts missing, 3=artifact corrupt, 4=no matching chunks'. This gives agents a clean branch without stderr parsing.

findings.title: lint tuning parameters (thresholds) have no CLI flags — agents cannot adjust sensitivity without code changes
findings.why_it_matters: run_lint_impl() accepts pairwise_threshold, duplicate_cosine, degenerate_l2, degenerate_nnz, levenshtein_ratio, target_chunk_chars, max_chunk_chars as keyword arguments with defaults, but run_lint() (the CLI handler) calls run_lint_impl(output_dir) with no overrides. An agent tuning corpus quality gates must either fork the code or accept the hardcoded defaults. Adding --duplicate-cosine, --max-chunk-chars, etc. as optional argparse flags with defaults matching the constants would give agents and CI pipelines per-invocation control.
evidence: lint.py:288-293: run_lint() passes no keyword args to run_lint_impl(), all tuning params use hardcoded defaults
lint.py:25-29: constants DEFAULT_LINT_PAIRWISE_THRESHOLD=2000, DEFAULT_DUPLICATE_COSINE=0.95 etc. defined but not exposed as flags
findings.suggested_fix: In _add_lint(), add optional flags: `p.add_argument('--duplicate-cosine', type=float, default=DEFAULT_DUPLICATE_COSINE)`, `p.add_argument('--max-chunk-chars', type=int, default=1500)`, `p.add_argument('--pairwise-threshold', type=int, default=DEFAULT_LINT_PAIRWISE_THRESHOLD)`. Pass them from run_lint() to run_lint_impl(). This is idiomatic argparse with defaults defined as module constants.

residual_risks: The ANSI / terminal color risk is not present in this codebase (no color library used, all output is plain print()). However if a logging handler with colored formatters is added upstream, all subcommands share stderr and could emit ANSI to pipes. A NO_COLOR env-var check in a shared logging setup would pre-empt this.

ingest is effectively idempotent via atomic swap + manifest caching, but there is no --dry-run flag. An agent that wants to preview the operation without writing cannot do so without inspecting internals.

The identity banner (IDENTITY_BANNER constant) is present in description= but is not emitted to stdout/stderr at runtime for ingest. Plan R9 mentions a parseable banner on ingest start; the current implementation only shows it in --help output.
testing_gaps: No test exercises run_query() with non-TTY stdout to verify that structured output (once added) is correct and complete.
No test asserts that lint exit codes match the fatal/warning/success contract from the plan (fatal=2, warning=1, success=0). Current tests likely pass with the broken 0/1 mapping.
No test verifies that all ingest error paths (exit codes 2-10) produce a non-empty error message on stderr.
